results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the VFB database. VFB records show that the mushroom body is divided into these three parts, with the calyx receiving sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus being a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes, and the mushroom body lobe system consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch. VFB holds various records related to the mushroom body, including [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body, and [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ExpressionOverlapsHere "Run in VFB: Expression patterns overlapping mushroom body") expression patterns overlapping the mushroom body. For further information, you can explore the available VFB data, such as the neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body or the tracts/nerves innervating the mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type is a type of neuron in the fly brain with specific characteristics and functions. According to VFB, it has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer, as described by Klapoetke et al. (2017). This arrangement allows it to detect looming (expansion) stimuli. In the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4, as reported by Wu et al. (2016) and Tanaka and Clark (2022). Its arbors span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells, as noted by Wu et al. (2016). The LPLC2 projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4, as described by Wu et al. (2016). 

VFB records show that the LPLC2 visual neuron type is connected to various neuron types, including sensory system neurons, visual system neurons, and projection neurons, with 610 downstream class-connectivity partners found. The activity of LPLC2 elicits a jump escape response, as reported by Wu et al. (2016) and Klapoetke et al. (2017). VFB holds information that there are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe, as noted by Wu et al. (2016), and they are cholinergic, as reported by Davis et al. (2020).

results.question: How many distinct neuron types are currently classified within the adult Drosophila visual system, and how are they organised hierarchically?

Additionally, for [neuron 30721 (FANC:564024)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_001028l9 "Open neuron 30721 (FANC:564024) in Virtual Fly Brain"), VFB has annotated [8](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=VFB_001028l9,SimilarMorphologyTo "Run in VFB: Find similar neurons to neuron 30721 (FANC:564024)") similar neurons that can be found through the "Find similar neurons" query. You can use these queries as a starting point to explore the FAFB and FANC CATMAID datasets within Virtual Fly Brain.

results.title: Anatomy teaching diagrams
results.question: Is there a circuit diagram of the mushroom body available on Virtual Fly Brain?
results.response: VFB holds various data related to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"), including neurons with some part in the mushroom body, neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body, and parts of the mushroom body. However, I could not find any information that specifically indicates the availability of a circuit diagram of the mushroom body on Virtual Fly Brain. VFB does have images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, but it is unclear if these images constitute a circuit diagram. The user may want to explore the available data, such as the [22137](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in mushroom body") images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, to see if they can be used to infer circuit information.
